title: Metadata ledger sync sleuth — onprem control plane inconsistency
content:
TL;DR:
We saw intermittent tenant control-plane divergence on on-prem deployments (two tenants reported API errors and stale route state for ~3-8 minutes). Root hypothesis: metadata ledger replication lag between control-plane instances combined with a failing compact/GC job that left partial tombstones. This caused some edge proxies to read stale mapping and fail healthcheck updates, producing cascading session affinity fluctuation.

Impact:
- Affected: 2 enterprise customers in EU-onprem region (tenant-a, tenant-b).
- Symptoms: API key lookups returning 404 for active keys, routing table stale (old ip:port), healthchecks marked instances unhealthy, client reconnect churn.
- Duration: recurring windows between 2027-03-21T02:14Z and 2027-03-21T05:22Z (most severe at 02:14-02:26Z).
- Customer-visible: 3–5 min request errors, reconnects; no data loss observed, but spike in error-rates and latency.

Immediate detection:
- Alert: controlplane-metadata-consistency-ms > 1200ms (firing). Alert origin: onprem-metrics-exporter -> SRE alert rule (threshold tuned).
- Pager duty: Eng oncall (Tom) triaged from 02:18Z.

High-level timeline (abridged):
- 02:12Z: First anomaly spikes in metadata replication latency metric for eu-onprem-cluster-3.
- 02:14Z: Tenant-A reports API key lookup failures (CS ticket created).
- 02:16Z: Pager duty alert fires. Tom pulls logs, notices repeated WAL-apply errors.
- 02:20Z: Workaround applied: restart metadata-replicator process on node-7 (temporary drop in replication lag).
- 02:26Z: Errors reduce but similar blips occur 03:10Z and 04:38Z.
- 02:40Z: Found evidence of GC/compact job failing to process tombstones; backlog of ~14k tombstones.
- 04:20Z: Manual compaction run triggered (low-traffic window), replication backlog cleared.
- 05:22Z: System stabilized, alerts recovered.

Relevant logs (snippets):
- 2027-03-21T02:15:41Z [replicator] WARN apply_wal: write failed: "partial write: tombstone missing seq=112345"
- 2027-03-21T02:15:42Z [proxy] ERROR route_lookup: cache_miss for tenant-a key=ak_***; falling back to remote lookup
- 2027-03-21T02:15:45Z [health] WARN check_update: instance=ip-10-9-2-45 stale-state (last_seen=2027-03-21T02:09:18Z)
- 2027-03-21T02:40:02Z [gc] ERROR compact_job: caught I/O error during compaction at segment-87 -> skipping segment

Reproducible pattern and hypotheses:
1) Ledger replication lag combined with broken compaction creates short windows where reads see inconsistent tombstone state leading to:
   - read_path: missing key -> proxy returns 404 for existing keys
   - route path: stale mapping -> healthchecks stop updating
2) The compaction failure is I/O related but only on specific local storage devices (nvme-2) in node-7; other nodes operated normally.
3) The replication mechanism lacks a robust fallback when a replica falls behind while compaction removes segments on the leader, leaving replicas unable to fetch older WAL frames.

Diagnostics run (commands & quick findings):
- curl -s http://controlplane.local:8080/health => OK on master, WARN on node-7
- rplctl status --cluster eu-onprem-cluster-3 => replicating: node-7 lag=2m13s; backlog=14200 msgs
- du -h /var/lib/ledger/segments | sort -h => segment-87 ~23GB (largest), filesystem /dev/nvme2 showing 85% used
- strace compact-worker PID 4921 => intermittent EIO on write syscall at offsets matching segment-87
- journalctl -u nvme-monitor => firmware-reported recovery on nvme-2 around 2027-03-20T23:49Z (possible underlying hardware flakiness)

Short-term mitigations (what we did):
- Restarted metadata-replicator on node-7 to force re-streaming from leader (reduced lag temporarily). Owner: Tom (oncall).
- Scaled up temporary read-replicas to absorb read load for tenant lookups. Owner: Priya.
- Manual compaction with --skip-corrupt option to allow GC to progress (cleared backlog). Owner: Luis.
- Customer comms: CS informed affected customers with timeline and apology.

Persistent/Long-term fixes proposed (runbook + infra changes):
1) Short-term (within 2 weeks):
   - Add guardrails to compaction to avoid deleting segments that might be required by lagging replicas (config flag: compaction.safe_window_seconds). Owner: eng-private-deployments (Anika).
   - Improve replicator logic to detect EIOs and throttle compaction on leader or pause segment deletion until all replicas have applied. Owner: serving-runtime team.
   - Replace nvme-2 drives on node-7 and run SMART/firmware updates across cluster. Owner: infra (hardware ops).
2) Medium-term (1–2 months):
   - Implement incremental snapshotting for slower replicas to catch up without requiring full WAL replays.
   - Add a cross-node checksum/verification step to replication to detect partial-tombstone states earlier.
   - Enhance alerting: separate alerts for replication-lag-backlog-size and compaction-failure-count. Current single metric masks root cause.
3) Long-term (3+ months):
   - Revisit metadata ledger architecture (sharding / quorum model) to avoid single-segment GC implications.

Runbook draft: "Onprem metadata divergence - quick playbook"
(Goal: restore serve-read consistency within 15m while minimizing customer impact)
- Step 0 (diagnose):
  - rplctl status --cluster <cluster> => check lag/backlog.
  - check compact_job last run: journalctl -u compact-worker | tail -n50.
  - probe storage health: smartctl -a /dev/nvme2; dmesg | grep nvme.
- Step 1 (isolate):
  - If compact_job failing and backlog > 10k => mark cluster in limited-mode: block new compaction deletions and enable read-replicas. (runbook command: ctl cluster mode set <cluster> limited-compaction)
- Step 2 (mitigate):
  - Restart replicator on lagging node(s) in controlled rolling fashion (restart one replicator at a time).
  - If restart doesn't reduce lag within 5m => spin up replica-helper with snapshot-boot (ctl replicator helper start --from-leader).
- Step 3 (repair):
  - Run manual compaction with --skip-corrupt AND --verify-checksums, then monitor rplctl backlog.
  - If EIO persists => cordon node, replace NVMe, and rehydrate replica from snapshot.
- Step 4 (post-recovery):
  - Run data-consistency check: ctl ledger verify --cluster <cluster> --window 00:10:00.
  - Fire customer recovery notes and postmortem template.

Monitoring and alert changes proposed:
- New metrics: ledger.compaction.error_count, ledger.segment.corrupt_count, ledger.replica.backlog_messages.
- Alert thresholds: backlog > 10000 => P1 to oncall (auto escalates); compaction.error_count > 3 in 5m => P2.
- Add a synthetic check: controlplane-key-lookup-synthetic for a test-tenant that runs every 30s and validates route+api-key resolution.

Open follow-ups / action items (owners):
- Anika: draft compaction.safe_window_seconds RFC + config default (due 2027-03-29).
- Priya: add replica-helper snapshot bootstrap flow to runbook and test in staging (due 2027-04-05).
- Luis: coordinate hardware replacement for node-7 and schedule SMART sweeping across cluster (due 2027-03-28).
- Tom: expand alerts with backlog and compaction error metrics (due 2027-03-25).
- SRE: run 2 rehearsals of the runbook on staging next two oncall rotations.

Notes to self / informal observations:
- The EIOs and firmware-recovery on nvme-2 before the incident feel suspicious — hardware flakiness probably triggered compaction failure which cascaded. Need to push infra to treat nvme errors as urgent P0.
- We should avoid doing "blind compaction" on leaders without verifying replica offsets. This is a classic window where GC meets slow follower -> data not yet available.
- Customers were pretty calm thanks to CS early head-up. Kudos to Priya for coordination.

Unresolved questions:
- Why did the leader decision to delete segment-87 proceed while replica lag > retention window? (race condition in compaction controller)
- Is there a hidden bug in WAL apply path that treats missing tombstones as partial write instead of retrying?

Attachments to include in postmortem: raw replicator logs (02:10-06:00), compact-worker logs, nvme SMART dumps for node-7, rplctl status captures, customer error traces.

Draft postmortem title suggestion: "Onprem metadata ledger compaction + NVMe flake -> transient control-plane divergence (2027-03-21)"

---
1-line retrospective: hardware flake exposed a compaction/replication race that allowed tombstone segments to be deleted before slow replicas replayed them; fix by adding compaction safety window and more robust replica catch-up paths.

End of notes.
